slides.3.title: Fortification Timing: A Precise Balance of Residual Sugar and Alcohol
slides.3.html:
Port's distinctive sweetness comes from the precise control of fortification timing. The winemaker must add grape spirit at exactly the right moment to halt fermentation.

🔬 Fermentation Monitoring

  • After harvest, fermentation begins in the Lagar or in fermentation vats
  • Sugar level (Baumé) and alcohol are measured every 2–4 hours
  • When natural alcohol reaches 6–8% (residual sugar of about 80–120 g/L), 77% neutral grape spirit is added
  • The spirit kills the yeast and fermentation stops immediately, giving a final alcohol of 19–22%

🎯 Fortification Ratio

  • Typically 1 part spirit is added to every 4 parts of grape juice (must) (a 1:4 ratio)
  • The final blend reaches 19–22% alcohol, inhibiting all microbial activity

⚖️ Controlling Sweetness

  • Earlier fortification (lower alcohol, 6%) → more residual sugar, sweeter (suited to Vintage Port)
  • Later fortification (8% alcohol) → less residual sugar, relatively drier (suited to Tawny)
  • The winemaker chooses the timing precisely according to the intended style
slides.4.title: Lagar: The Art of Treading in Traditional Stone Troughs
slides.4.html:
The Lagar is the Douro's traditional shallow granite trough, and foot treading is one of the most important techniques in the history of Port.

🏺 Structure and Dimensions of a Lagar

  • A shallow granite trough, about 60–90 cm deep and 3–5 m wide
  • The low height lets workers stand and tread comfortably without damaging the grape seeds
  • Each Lagar holds about 5,000–15,000 litres

🦶 Treading Procedure

  • First stage (2 hours of "cutting"): workers stand side by side, treading rhythmically to break the skins thoroughly
  • Second stage (resting stage): the skins are left to rise freely, and are trodden periodically to keep the cap moist
  • The whole process lasts 2–3 days until fortification

💎 Quality Advantages of the Lagar

  • The gentlest extraction: the weight and softness of human feet do not crush the seeds (which contain harsh tannins)
  • Efficient colour extraction: anthocyanin extraction is maximised within the short fermentation period (2–3 days)
  • Fine tannins: the delicate palate of top Vintage Port depends on Lagar treading
  • The top Quintas of the Symington group (Graham's・Dow's・Warre's) still insist on the Lagar
slides.5.title: Traditional Lagar Treading vs. Modern Mechanical Treading
slides.5.items.0.label: Traditional Lagar (by foot)
slides.5.items.0.desc: The gentlest extraction: seeds are not crushed, giving fine tannins and rich colour. Essential for top Vintage Port. Costly, so only suitable for small batches
slides.5.items.1.label: Robotic Lagar (mechanical feet)
slides.5.items.1.desc: Silicone mechanical feet imitate human treading. Pioneered by Niepoort and Churchill in the 2000s, it gives quality close to a traditional Lagar and can handle large batches
slides.5.items.2.label: Autovinificator (automatic pump-over)
slides.5.items.2.desc: A traditional large-volume system: CO₂ pressure from fermentation pumps the wine over the top of the cap for circulating maceration. Efficient, but extracts less than treading
slides.5.items.3.label: Piston System (piston plunging)
slides.5.items.3.desc: Hydraulic pistons push the cap down at set intervals. Gentler than an Autovinificator, and a common choice for mid-quality Port
slides.6.question: When is grape spirit (fortification) usually added during Port production?
slides.6.options.1: Immediately after the grapes are picked and pressed
slides.6.options.2: When fermentation reaches about 7–8% natural alcohol
slides.6.explanation: Port is fortified when fermentation has reached about 7–8% natural alcohol (roughly 2–3 days into fermentation). The 77% grape spirit added at this point kills the yeast and halts fermentation, retaining a large amount of residual sugar (about 80–120 g/L) and creating Port's distinctive sweet fortified style.
slides.7.question: What is the main quality advantage of traditional Lagar treading over modern mechanical fermentation?
slides.7.options.1: Human feet are the gentlest, do not crush the seeds, and extract fine tannins and rich colour
slides.7.explanation: The key advantage of the Lagar is that the weight and softness of human feet are just right for breaking the skins without crushing the seeds. Seeds contain harsh, green tannins, and crushing them lowers the quality of the Port. Lagar treading therefore maximises colour extraction within the short fermentation period (2–3 days) while keeping the tannins fine, making it the essential method for top Vintage Port.
